name: styleforge
long_description: Maintain isolated writing-style libraries for one or more authors in any language. Ingest new corpus with deduplication and snapshots. Get on-demand writing guides via MCP tools and `/style-write` slash commands. Includes feedback intake and rollback for misingested corpus.

data_dir.title: Data directory
data_dir.description: Where styleforge stores authors, corpus, snapshots, and changelog (default: ~/.styleforge). The server also needs to read source files from arbitrary paths during ingest, so this must NOT be sandboxed.

tools.name: list_authors
tools.description: List all writing-style authors registered in styleforge.

tools.name: create_author
tools.description: Register a new author with a slug and display name.

tools.name: delete_author
tools.description: Permanently delete an author and all their data. Requires explicit confirmation.

tools.name: get_writing_guide
tools.description: Return the complete writing guide for a given author: SKILL_OVERLAY + style-patterns + learned-rules. Call this BEFORE writing in an author's style.

tools.name: sample_corpus
tools.description: Return 1-5 corpus entries from an author, optionally filtered by topic. Bucketed sampling avoids over-representing any single topic.

tools.name: ingest_dryrun
tools.description: Inspect files for ingest without writing. Returns lists of new files, exact duplicates, near-duplicates, and errors. ALWAYS call this before ingest_execute and show the result to the user.

tools.name: ingest_execute
tools.description: Actually ingest files into an author's corpus. Creates a snapshot before writing. Refuses near-duplicates unless allow_near is set.

tools.name: record_pattern_evidence
tools.description: After viewing an ingested article, record its topic tags and which style-patterns it exhibits. This is how an author's style fingerprint accumulates.

tools.name: append_observation
tools.description: Append a candidate-pattern observation to observations.md. Use for novel patterns spotted in a single article that aren't yet in the rule catalog. Stays as observation until cross-corpus stability earns promotion.

tools.name: recompute_stats
tools.description: Recompute pattern frequencies from corpus-index.json. Run after record_pattern_evidence calls.

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Show corpus size, topic breakdown, and pattern frequencies for an author.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Manually create a snapshot of an author's mutable state.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List all snapshots for an author, with timestamps and labels.

tools.name: rollback
tools.description: Restore an author's state from a snapshot. Saves current state as a new snapshot first, so rollback-of-rollback works.

tools.name: record_feedback
tools.description: Append a feedback entry about a recent style-write output.

tools.name: get_feedback_log
tools.description: Read the feedback log for an author.

tools.name: apply_learned_rule
tools.description: After style-feedback skill negotiates a learned rule with the user, persist it to learned-rules.md. Requires user-confirmed rule text.

prompts.name: style-write
prompts.description: Write or rewrite a piece in a specific author's style.
prompts.text:
I want you to write in the style of a specific styleforge author.

1. Call `list_authors`. If there's only one, use it. Otherwise ask which one.
2. Call `get_writing_guide` for that slug. Read the returned guide carefully.
3. Optionally call `sample_corpus` (k=2-3) for grounding examples.
4. Ask the user what they want written (if they haven't already said).
5. Draft the piece. Replicate STRUCTURE / SYNTAX / RHETORIC ONLY. Do NOT import the author's political stance unless explicitly requested. The user's stated stance always wins.
6. Self-check against the §4 "failure modes" section of style-patterns.md.
7. Deliver. Then briefly ask: "Satisfied? If not, tell me what's off and I'll log it via record_feedback."

prompts.name: style-ingest
prompts.description: Ingest new articles into an author's corpus. Provide local file paths.
prompts.text:
Ingest articles into a styleforge author's corpus.

1. Call `list_authors`. If there's only one, use it. Otherwise ask.
2. Ask for local file paths on the user's machine. Files must be accessible from the local filesystem.
3. Batch limit: 5 files. Split larger batches.
4. Call `ingest_dryrun`. Show: new_files / exact_duplicates / near_duplicates. If near-dups, ask: (a) treat as new, (b) skip, (c) cancel.
5. After confirmation, call `ingest_execute` with a descriptive `message` parameter.
6. Enrichment: for each new entry, read the source, call `record_pattern_evidence` with topics + pattern_ids. Novel patterns go through `append_observation`.
7. Call `recompute_stats`.
8. Report: ingested count, snapshot id, rollback hint.

prompts.name: style-feedback
prompts.description: Digest accumulated feedback into actionable learned-rules.
prompts.text:
Process accumulated feedback for a styleforge author.

1. Call `list_authors`. If there's only one, use it. Otherwise ask.
2. Call `get_feedback_log` to read all entries.
3. Call `create_snapshot` with label `pre-feedback-review`.
4. Group recurring failure modes. Contradictory feedback: show to user, don't auto-resolve.
5. Present proposed learned-rules: trigger / corrective_action / confidence.
6. Wait for user accept/reject/edit on each.
7. For accepted proposals, call `apply_learned_rule`.
8. Report: K accepted, K rejected, snapshot id.

prompts.name: style-rollback
prompts.description: Roll back an author's state to a previous snapshot.
prompts.text:
Help the user roll back a styleforge author to a previous state.

1. Call `list_authors`. If there's only one, use it. Otherwise ask.
2. Call `list_snapshots`.
3. Present numbered list (newest first) with timestamp and label/message.
4. Ask user which to restore.
5. Call `rollback`. Report success and pre-rollback snapshot name.

prompts.name: style-authors
prompts.text: Call `list_authors` and present the results as a concise table (slug, display name).

prompts.name: style-stats
prompts.description: Show corpus statistics for a styleforge author.
prompts.text:
Show statistics for a styleforge author.

1. Call `list_authors`. If there's only one, use it. Otherwise ask.
2. Call `get_stats`.
3. Present: entry count, topic breakdown, pattern frequencies, sample_warning if applicable.
